title: response-format negotiator: route-level strict toggle and diagnostic-id passthrough
author: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a route-scoped response_format negotiator and per-route strict-mode toggle with diagnostic-id passthrough to improve developer visibility when schema validation fails. Motivation: customers running mixed workloads need fine-grained control over schema strictness per API route and better cross-system observability for invalid-response incidents. This change adds: 1) a runtime layer that inspects the incoming response_format header (and legacy openai-style schema hints) and selects a route-specific enforcement policy; 2) a per-route toggle persisted in route metadata that can be set to permissive/soft/strict, with strict enforcing immediate stream rewind+reject and permissive allowing best-effort coercion; 3) a short-lived diagnostic_id token emitted on validation failures that flows through streaming checkpoints so the Console can link SLOs, traces and example prompts to a single incident ID; 4) OpenAI-compatibility shim updates to accept legacy "response_format":"json_schema" hints and map them to the new negotiator semantics; 5) small client-facing error code changes (RFCVAL-01..03) and human-friendly messages for common mis-validation cases; 6) unit and integration tests that exercise streaming checkpoint resume semantics and route policy precedence. Backwards compatibility: default behavior for routes that do not opt in remains unchanged (current permissive fallback). Rollout plan: opt-in toggle exposed in Console UI and Admin API, initial beta enabled for internal staging, then staged customer rollout. Related: addresses SUP-1124 support request and ties to ENG-3481 quality RFE.

Emit diagnostic_id on validation failures and propagate to streaming checkpoints: runtime/streaming_checkpoint.rs

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Can you clarify precedence when a client sends an explicit header but the route is configured to strict? Which wins?
Aisha Patel: Route config takes precedence. Updated description and doc to be explicit. If route is strict we log an INFO about header override.
Liam O'Connor: Streaming checkpoint propagation looks good but I worry about perf when emitting diagnostic_id for every minor validation warning. Can we reserve diagnostic ids for failures only?

Aisha Patel: Diagnostic IDs are only emitted for validation failures that result in either a parse error or schema mismatch above threshold. Minor coercions are logged locally without diagnostic-id emission.
Ravi Deshpande: Please add a migration note for customers using openai-compat that rely on legacy behavior. Also add an admin knex migration for route metadata column.
Aisha Patel: Added migration file and expanded docs with explicit migration steps.
release_notes: Added route-level response_format negotiation with per-route strict/permissive modes and diagnostic-id passthrough for schema validation incidents. New error codes RFCVAL-01..03. A Console toggle and Admin API were added to manage route policies.
testing_notes: Integration harness includes a faulty-schema generator that intentionally emits partial JSON in stream to validate checkpoint resume and diagnostic-id correlation. Verified diagnostics link to trace IDs in Console staging cluster.
rollout_plan: Feature hidden behind "routeSchemaNegotiator" feature-flag. Enable for internal staging on 2026-02-26, invite beta customers in week of 2026-03-09, full rollout after two weeks of monitoring.
notes_for_ops: Ops should monitor metrics: schema.validation.failures, diagnostic_id.emitted, stream.resume.rate. Alert if stream.resume.rate > 0.5% during rollout. If regressions seen, flip route-level toggle to permissive for affected tenants.
human_friendly_errors: RFCVAL-01: response does not conform to schema: missing required property. Provide example payload and diagnostic_id for follow-up.
RFCVAL-02: response type mismatch: expected array but got string. Offers coercion suggestions when possible.
RFCVAL-03: streaming parse error: truncated JSON detected. Stream was rewinded and rejected in strict mode; provide checkpoint token to resume in permissive mode.
